newsitem.title: HAITI: Cuba re-opens embassy in Haiti after 30 years.
newsitem.headline: Cuba re-opens embassy in Haiti after 30 years.

text.p: Cuban Ambassador Oscar Coet Blackstock presented his credentials to President Rene Preval on Wednesday, creating the first Cuban diplomatic mission in Haiti in more than 30 years.
"This is a relationship that will contribute to the life of Haitians," said Coet Blackstock. "We don't have the intent of damaging Haiti's relationship with any other country."
The United States, which has maintained a trade embargo against Cuba for more than three decades, said it respected Haiti's right to establish diplomatic relations.

"However it is the position of the U.S. government that any upgrade in relations with Cuba will be taken by the Cuban government as proof that its systematic denial of human rights at home is not an obstacle to improved relations with its neighbours in the region," the U.S. embassy in Port-au-Prince said in a statement.

Haitian Foreign Ministry adviser Kleber Vielot said the agreement to re-open a Cuban embassy in Haiti had been in the works over the past year, and the Haitian government had not yet felt any pressure from the United States on the matter.
On Monday Prime Minister Rosny Smarth cited new relations with Cuba and Russia to counter concerns by parliamentarians that Haiti was too dependent on the United States.
About 300 U.S. troops are still in Haiti, left from a 1994 intervention to restore President Jean-Bertrand Aristide to power after a 1991 military coup.
Cuban-Haitian diplomatic ties were cut in the 1960s by then-President Francois Duvalier.
